text: ABSTRACT

runs.text: ABSTRACT

text: Shopzy is a full-stack, production-grade web application that addresses the everyday problem faced by urban consumers — the inability to quickly discover nearby local shops and compare the prices they charge for the same item. Consumers currently rely on word-of-mouth, physical visits, or fragmented social-media posts to locate shops and assess whether a price is fair. There is no unified digital channel that combines shop discovery, real-time price transparency, and actionable contact options in a single interface.

runs.text: Shopzy is a full-stack, production-grade web application that addresses the everyday problem faced by urban consumers — the inability to quickly discover nearby local shops and compare the prices they charge for the same item. Consumers currently rely on word-of-mouth, physical visits, or fragmented social-media posts to locate shops and assess whether a price is fair. There is no unified digital channel that combines shop discovery, real-time price transparency, and actionable contact options in a single interface.

text: Shopzy solves this by providing a geospatial search engine that locates shops within a user-defined radius, ranks them by a composite relevance score, and — critically — allows a user to search by item name (e.g., "Haircut", "1 kg Basmati rice") and receive a ranked list of nearby shops with that item's price, from cheapest to most expensive, together with computed savings over the category average.

runs.text: Shopzy solves this by providing a geospatial search engine that locates shops within a user-defined radius, ranks them by a composite relevance score, and — critically — allows a user to search by item name (e.g., "Haircut", "1 kg Basmati rice") and receive a ranked list of nearby shops with that item's price, from cheapest to most expensive, together with computed savings over the category average.

text: The platform serves three actor types: Customers (discover, compare, review), Shop Owners (list and manage their business, publish a price list, track analytics), and Administrators (verify shops, moderate content, monitor platform health). The backend is a Node.js/Express REST API written in TypeScript, backed by MongoDB with a 2dsphere geospatial index, and accelerated by a Redis cache layer. The frontend is a React 18 single-page application built with Vite and styled with Tailwind CSS. The entire stack is containerised with Docker, enforces strict security practices aligned to the OWASP Top 10, and ships with 89 automated integration tests.

text: MOTIVATION

runs.text: MOTIVATION

text: The informal retail economy of Indian cities is large and vibrant, yet almost entirely invisible online. A kirana store, a salon, a tiffin service, or a hardware shop rarely has a website, an accurate Google Business profile, or any public price list. Consumers therefore cannot comparison-shop before they leave their homes, and small business owners have no affordable channel to advertise their prices or promotions to a local audience.

text: •  No trust layer. There is no platform specific to local businesses where verified reviews, ratings, and owner-replied feedback accumulate to build consumer trust.

text: •  Digital exclusion of small businesses. Building even a basic website is beyond the budget and skill set of many micro-business owners. A platform where listing, updating a price list, and tracking customer engagement requires only a smartphone reduces this barrier.
